11.text: Usually one vertical crack is formed, with

12.text: various ramifications above and below. The

13.text: following principles are applied for their expla-

14.text: nation. Everything that comes from the sea is

15.text: good, even though it be from under the supposed

16.text: level of the ground: “Nothing evil comes from

17.text: the sea.” Indications from the underground, or

18.text: “bottom of the bone,” on the contrary, are of

22.text: If there is produced only one vertical line,

23.text: it is a favorable indication; but if this line is short, or, on the contrary, if

24.text: it reaches the very edge of the bone, the indications are unfavorable. Should

25.text: the bone burn too quickly, it is likewise unfavorable. The small cross-lines

26.text: not reaching up to the principal crack, when in the upper region, foretell

27.text: only news of something; while the longer lines, crossing the principal crack,

28.text: foretell the arrival of the thing. A large cross zigzag line foretells greatness

29.text: of the thing which will come. For instance, a detached cross-line from the

30.text: “mountain” may signify news about wild reindeer; a longer line, the coming

31.text: of wild reindeer; and a zigzag line, the abundance of the wild reindeer; etc.

32.text: A cross-line from the “bottom of the bone” foretells an attack by wolves, or

33.text: the arrival of the “spirit of disease,” or even death. A line formed on the

34.text: top of the principal crack signifies a snow-storm; a semicircular line on

35.text: the same place signifies unexpected death. A detached line in the region of

36.text: the “sea” signifies some unexpected news. Thus, for instance, cracks on the

37.text: shoulder-blade represented in Fig. 298 indicate (1) abundance of some game

38.text: coming from the mountain, evidently reindeer, because it was the season for

39.text: the reindeer-hunt; (2) the coming of wolves to the herd of the camp.
